label: Appetitive power following apprehension: A soul's power for appetitively relating to what it…
definition: A soul's power for appetitively relating to what it apprehends as suitable or good, beyond inclination fixed by its own natural form. This is a power/capacity description and does not require an actual current episode or an absent good.
note: Owner-selected relational interpretation (2026-11-09): Capacity specifies subject-relative possible appetitive responses following suitable OR good apprehension. Seeking requires absence; love, delight and possible communication require possession. Possibility is an explicitly primitive appetitive ability, independent of mere cognition and actual acts. Universal responsiveness remains open. Capacity.Possessed separately admits a soul with a nonempty response relation; an empty specification asserts no possession. The quantifier witnesses some possible response at some occasion, not a current exercise. Concrete recognition of the relation as appetitive, its soul-power applicability and recognition by HasWill remain open semantic obligations. This interface is not the finite ranked one-end configuration and does not identify creaturely passive capacity with divine willing. Full-body binding audit (2026-11-09): the declaration is Capacity.Possessed, parameterized by supplied relational Capacity content, because the unchanged body describes a soul's power rather than an arbitrary possible-response specification. This predicate admits exactly soulhood and some possible appetitive response; it does not require current exercise or universal responsiveness. The content interface remains Capacity. This corrects the shared definition anchor consistently in both disambiguations; old primitive consumers remain unmigrated.
